monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR — though total volume and pace have declined versus last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 rose from 55% to 83% while Z4 dropped from 15% to 1%, indicating a strategic de-load or aerobic base emphasis.

goal_tracker.message: You need 3.7 more km across 2 remaining sessions to match last month’s volume — e.g., one 2.0 km easy run and one 1.7 km Zone 2 tempo.

insights.title: Efficiency slightly decreased despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.37 km/hr per bpm — meaning each heart beat now propels ~0.3% less distance than last month, likely due to recent slower pacing (avg pace slowed by 28 sec/km) and reduced Z3+Z4 stimulus.

insights.title: Near-complete absence of threshold and VO2 max work this month
insights.body: Z4 dropped from 15% to 1% and Z5 disappeared entirely (0%), while Z1+Z2 now dominate at 83% — a meaningful departure from last month’s balanced stimulus (Z3+Z4+Z5 = 45%).

insights.title: Cadence improved but stride length variability increased
insights.body: Cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm (+3), yet stride length swung from 66.5 cm (May 6) to 94.4 cm (May 16) — a 27.9 cm range — suggesting inconsistent effort distribution or form breakdown under faster efforts.

insights.title: Strong recovery signature in longest run
insights.body: The May 6 long run (9.5 km, avg HR 131 bpm, pace 10:33 min/km) stayed fully in Z1–Z2 with 3.0 Aerobic TE — indicating excellent autonomic resilience and readiness for sustained aerobic load.

recommendations.action: Do a 4.0 km Zone 3 run (HR 145–152 bpm) at consistent pace (~8:30–8:45 min/km) on your next midweek run.
recommendations.reason: To restore threshold stimulus missing this month (Z3 dropped from 26% to 15%, Z4 vanished); your May 16 run hit 148 bpm at 7:27 min/km — proving you can sustain Z3 when focused.

recommendations.action: Add 3 × 1-min cadence drills (160+ spm) before your next two runs, focusing on quick turnover without overstriding.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved overall (+3 spm), but May 16’s 94.4 cm stride (vs. 66.5 cm on May 6) suggests overstriding at speed — drills will reinforce neuromuscular control.

recommendations.action: Repeat the May 6 long-run structure: 9.0–9.5 km at ≤133 bpm, aiming for pace ≤10:30 min/km, with HR staying ≤5 bpm above Z2 ceiling.
recommendations.reason: That session delivered optimal aerobic TE (3.0) and low stress (GCT 351 ms, VO₂ max stable at 36.0) — ideal for reinforcing endurance foundation.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild sustainable Z3 capacity while preserving your strong Z1–Z2 aerobic base — using HR-guided pacing and cadence discipline to improve efficiency and reduce vertical oscillation drift.
